note: The eight lines the project closed, as inputs rather than as prose. Each case names the gate the line is recorded as binding on, where the numbers came from, and every input the arithmetic needs. `tools/viability.py` re-derives the quotients, checks that the first gate to fire is the recorded one, and refuses an optimistic bound read as an opening. The `also` entries are recorded and printed but never gated: a second kill is not the binding one, and an exclusion is not a quotient.

also: docs/RETROSPECTIVE.md:90 -- the line is recorded as a fee that is a multiple of the spread the venue offers, so a quote cannot pay for itself at any width
docs/DESIGN_REVIEW.md:411 -- pairs the same 2.57 against 0.095 on the mainline window, and the kill does not depend on which of the two windows is quoted
docs/PERFORMANCE_HISTORY.md:1979 -- a contract pays about 0.62 USD of commission against a tick worth 1.25, which is the half tick this divides by
docs/PERFORMANCE_HISTORY.md:2012 -- a fee a tick can cover is not the same thing as a capture a fee can pay for, and this is where the two came apart
